submission.natural_language_explanation: Broad layer-0 head: predict ordinary prose, code, numbers and names active-weak (content words, verbs, numbers and word pieces near a text's start reach 0.25-0.5 of max; a short plain sentence with no comma or article sits near the line, so about a third of those fall just below), and predict it strong (0.6-1.0 of max) on a comma or an English article (' the', ' a', ' an') within roughly the first five tokens of a text, where it attends mostly to itself; the same tokens fade with position and are usually below 0.5 of max past token 8 and near the line by token 12-14, so a late comma or article adds nothing over the surrounding content words. Non-article determiners (' this', ' my', ' her', ' some') and the connectives ' and', ' of', ' from', ' by' stay at 0-0.25 of max at any position, and short phrases built only of single-token particles (Up, down, In, out, On, off, Over, Back, forth, Through, Round, To, fro) joined by ' and' with no comma, article, noun or number are predicted inactive (near 0); adding a comma or 'the' + noun after such a chain makes it active.

rival_explanations: Position-free token reading: the head fires strongly on any comma or English article wherever it sits in a text, so a comma or ' the' at token 15-30 should be as strong as one at token 1-3.

Position-only reading: any token in a text's first five positions is strong whatever its identity, so early ' and', ' my', ' this' or particle chains like 'Up and down' should be as active as an early comma or article.
